To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we propose a novel method for Bayesian inference that is unbiased, computationally efficient and scalable to Big Data, (2) we demonstrate that this method can be applied to a range of statistical models, including those commonly used in the social sciences, and (3) we demonstrate the utility of our method in the context of real world problems

(i) a new methodology is proposed for unbiased estimation of expectations with respect to the posterior, (ii) it is applicable to many statistical models, (iii) the variance of the resulting estimators is controlled by the user, (iv) its computational complexity is sub-linear in data size, (v) it does not require explicit simulation from the posterior, and (vi) it is easy to implement

the proposed methodology provides unbiased estimation of expectations with respect to the posterior distribution, that it is provably unbiased and its variance is finite by design, that it is naturally scalable to large datasets, and that it is easy to tune and implement in a black box manner, without requiring access to the full posterior distribution.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how to estimate expectations with respect to a Bayesian posterior without having to simulate from it.
developing and analysing new computational methods that enable the application of Bayesian inference in Big Data settings.
a fundamental question in Bayesian inference: how to compute expectations of functions with regards to the posterior distribution.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our method is the first to provide a fully scalable and unbiased estimator for Bayesian expectations, with the potential to revolutionise Big Bayesian data analysis.
we have a method which is unbiased and converges to the desired tolerance, is scalable to big data and is computationally efficient.
we propose an efficient and accurate alternative to MCMC, which we call Unbiased Markov Chain Monte-Carlo (Unbiased MCMC).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a new methodology for Big Bayesian Data, which is provably unbiased and has a complexity that is sub-quadratic in the size of data.
we have constructed an unbiased estimator for a posterior distribution, which has a computational complexity sub-linear in the data size, and can be used for any Bayesian model.
we have constructed a new class of algorithms that are unbiased, computationally efficient, easy to tune and applicable to a large class of statistical models.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the problem of Bayesian inference can be solved in a computationally tractable manner without the need to simulate from the full posterior.
it is not necessary to simulate from the full posterior distribution to obtain an accurate approximation of expectations of interest.

the computational challenges of Bayesian statistics are not so much about simulation from a posterior distribution as it is about computing expectations of functions of interest with respect to the posterior.
